extracted.intended_audience: NLP researchers and ML engineers working on patent-domain language models and patent NLP
extracted.subtask_description: Designing, pretraining, and evaluating masked language models specifically for patent text, including corpus construction, tokenizer design, architecture/efficiency choices, training recipe, and downstream classification evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Architecture and Efficiency (ModernBERT adaptations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt the ModernBERT/FlexBERT design and incorporate recent training/architecture optimizations (e.g., FlashAttention, rotary embeddings, GLU feed-forward layers, Pre-LayerNorm with residual scaling).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These enhancements 'significantly reduce pretraining time and compute cost' while maintaining or improving model quality. Specific practices: 22 encoder blocks, hidden size 768 (base), 12 attention heads; remove dropout entirely for base variants; scale residual connections by 0.5; use GELU activation and apply LayerNorm at the beginning of each sublayer to improve stability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of FlashAttention and attention/kernel choices
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer FlashAttention-based attention kernels for efficiency and throughput where supported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FlashAttention enables larger batch sizes and longer sequences, yielding substantial training/inference throughput gains (reported 2.32× training and 3.55× inference vs PatentBERT aggregated). Note that throughput gains reflect both attention kernels and parameter counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Positional encoding choice (ALiBi / RoPE / rotary)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use ALiBi (attention with linear biases) or rotary/rope positional encodings instead of learned absolute position embeddings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ALiBi adds a relative position bias and enables generalization to longer sequences than seen in training. RoPE/rotary embeddings are used in some variants (e.g., RoPE θ settings reported) to support long contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feed-forward design: GLU expansions
rubrics_metrics.description: Implement feed-forward layers with a Gated Linear Unit (GLU) pattern where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GLU splits intermediate outputs and uses a gating signal to multiplicatively modulate the activated part; reported intermediate/G ELU/GLU expansion sizes for variants (e.g., GLU expansion to 2304 in VX; to 5248 in Mosaic-BERT-large).

rubrics_metrics.name: Tokenizer construction: BPE with domain-specific vocabulary
rubrics_metrics.description: Train a domain-specific BPE tokenizer (target 49,152 subwords) normalized by Unicode NFKC and lowercased; reserve special tokens [UNK],[PAD],[CLS],[SEP],[MASK].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-tokenization uses whitespace splitting; punctuation remains attached but may be segmented. BPE allowed frequent technical terms to appear as single tokens, improving MLM efficiency versus WordPiece in this work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tokenizer choice: BPE preferred over WordPiece for patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate subword/tokenizer algorithms; in this work BPE provided more efficient/compact representation and better downstream performance than WordPiece/section-aware variants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comparisons used average token entropy and unknown-token rates; BPE reduced MLM loss and increased masked token prediction accuracy in early training stages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vocabulary normalization practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Normalize input text using Unicode NFKC normalization followed by lowercasing to reduce sparsity and canonicalize characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This reduces case-induced sparsity and consolidates visually or canonically distinct code points; out-of-vocabulary sequences are mapped to [UNK].

rubrics_metrics.name: Fields retained for pretraining
rubrics_metrics.description: Retain abstracts, the first independent claim, and DWPI (where available) from patent records as the primary fields for pretraining.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-essential text (figure references, non-English characters) should be removed. Only the first independent claim per patent was retained to control input scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training data composition and provenance
rubrics_metrics.description: Construct a diverse corpus that blends public patent data with proprietary DWPI text rewritten by subject-matter experts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hybrid data helps the model generalize across patent categories and jurisdictions. Report final counts (e.g., ~64M patents, ~30.8B tokens; held-out test set of 3.4M patents ~1.6B tokens). Compare corpus size to baselines (e.g., about half of Google PatentBERT).

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-phase preprocessing pipeline (Phase 1 & Phase 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply Phase 1: extraction, basic normalization, family-level deduplication; then Phase 2: per-field FineWeb-inspired filtering and MinHash-based near-duplicate removal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Phase 1 keeps most-recent family representative; Phase 2 applies language filtering, repetition/quality heuristics, FineWeb-style filters, and MinHash LSH to remove near-duplicates. Document the pipeline, pseudocode, and intermediate sizes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language filtering
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply language identification to retain English-language patents only (fastText-based LID recommended).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filtering is applied per-field in Phase 2 to exclude non-English content prior to deduplication and reassembly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality and repetition filters
rubrics_metrics.description: Use MassiveText/Gopher-inspired heuristics and FineWeb-style quality filters to remove low-quality or repetitive documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement repetition/quality checks (e.g., Rae et al., 2021) per field; discard documents failing heuristics to improve pretraining signal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deduplication and near-duplicate removal (MinHash LSH)
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply MinHash-based fuzzy deduplication on 5-gram shingles with 64-bit hashes and a 14×8 banding scheme to cluster and remove near-duplicates, keeping one representative per cluster.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This step crucially reduced dataset size (e.g., from ~47.7B to ~31.6B tokens; −33.79%). Use DataTrove or similar libraries for signatures, bucketing, clustering and filtering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Masking probability for MLM
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a masking probability of 30% for masked language modeling pretraining.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recent findings indicate 15% (original BERT) is suboptimal; 30% was used here as more effective (citing Wettig et al., 2023).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pretraining objective: MLM-only
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the masked language modeling (MLM) objective and omit Next Sentence Prediction (NSP).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NSP was excluded as it provides minimal downstream benefit per cited literature (Liu et al., 2019; Izsak et al., 2021). Consider exploring complementary objectives (contrastive, span prediction, retrieval) in future work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optimizer choice and settings
rubrics_metrics.description: Use StableAdamW (an enhancement of AdamW incorporating per-parameter update clipping) for pretraining with settings (e.g., lr 3e-4 for base, β=(0.90,0.98), ε=1e-6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: StableAdamW aids stable low-precision training; report hyperparameters and any deviations across variants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learning rate schedule and warmup
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a linear warmup (6% of training steps) from 0 to peak learning rate (e.g., 3×10^-4) followed by linear decay for the remainder of training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This avoids initial instability; reported warmup fraction: 6%; final LR decays to ~2% of peak by the end of training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Batching and distributed training configuration
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a global batch size of 4096 sequences per step distributed across GPUs, with a micro-batch of 128 sequences per GPU and gradient synchronization across devices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training in experiments used 8×H100 GPUs. Document hardware and distributed strategy (Distributed DataParallel).

rubrics_metrics.name: Max sequence length and long-context support
rubrics_metrics.description: Set maximum sequence length appropriate to model variant: base variants used 1024 tokens; Mosaic-BERT-large supports up to 8192 tokens for long patent contexts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choice affects tokenizer/training efficiency and model suitability for long patent texts; ALiBi helps generalize to longer lengths than seen in training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model scaling experiments and naming (corpus suffixes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Train and compare multiple model sizes and corpus variants (e.g., ModernBERT-base-PT, ModernBERT-base-VX, Mosaic-BERT-large) and indicate corpus suffixes (-PT clean vs -VX raw).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: -PT indicates Phase 2 cleaned/near-deduplicated corpus; -VX indicates raw corpus prior to Phase 2 filtering. Report parameter counts (e.g., 149M base, 395M large) and differences in hyperparameters/optimizer scheduling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finetuning protocol and hyperparameters
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify finetuning optimizer, learning rates, epochs, seeds and other hyperparameters (e.g., adamw_torch_fused lr 3e-5 for some variants; 20 epochs; 4 seeds).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report per-dataset finetuning settings and use consistent seeds/epochs across model comparisons to ensure fair evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Downstream evaluation datasets and splits
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate on multiple patent classification datasets (WIPO, WIPOEC, HUPD, proprietary DatasetCLV), and report train/validation/test splits and label sets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include dataset statistics (counts per split), category label descriptions (appendix), and ensure consistent preprocessing for finetuning and evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation metrics and statistical reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Report downstream performance primarily via F1-scores (micro-averaged and per-dataset), masked accuracy and MLM loss for pretraining, and throughput measures for efficiency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present mean ± std across multiple runs (here, averages over 4 runs), include 95% confidence intervals estimated via Student's t distribution clipped to [0,1], and display per-dataset throughput (samples/sec) for training and inference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental repetition and seeds
rubrics_metrics.description: Run experiments multiple times with different random seeds and average results to quantify variance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This work ran four seeds per (dataset, model) and reported mean ± std; use multiple seeds to support statistical claims and compute confidence intervals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Throughput benchmarking (training & inference)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure and report training and inference throughput in samples/sec across datasets and models to quantify computational efficiency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report per-dataset mean ± std and macro-averaged values; attribute differences to attention kernels and model parameter counts when interpreting speedups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting reductions and dataset shrinkage
rubrics_metrics.description: Quantify dataset size reductions across preprocessing phases (documents and tokens) and report absolute/relative reductions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a summary table of reductions (e.g., Phase1: ≈150M → ≈70M patents; Phase2 tokens reduced ≈33.79%).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicitly state limitations such as English-only pretraining, MLM-only objective, limited compute budget compared to larger models, and limited downstream task scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use limitations to motivate future work (multilingual corpora, complementary objectives, scaling data/model, broader downstream tasks like retrieval/summarization/novelty detection).

rubrics_metrics.name: Tokenizer and model comparison reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: When comparing tokenizers/models, report pretraining loss curves, masked accuracy trajectories, downstream F1 across epochs, and which variant uses which tokenizer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include visualization (loss/accuracy/f1 curves) and describe observed behaviors (e.g., BPE tokenizer showed steeper decline in MLM loss and higher stabilized masked accuracy).

rubrics_metrics.name: Hyperparameter documentation and reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide detailed tables of pretraining and finetuning hyperparameters (optimizers, learning rates, β, ε, warmup, MLM masking, sliding windows, ALiBi start sizes, batch sizes, epochs, seeds).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document training hardware, train times, and distributed strategy (e.g., 8× H100; Distributed DataParallel) to aid reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation protocol fairness considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare models fairly by controlling for training data, tokenizer, architecture differences, and reporting when baselines used different pretraining corpora (e.g., PatentBERT trained on USPTO data).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note dataset/pretraining corpus overlaps and domain alignment effects (e.g., PatentBERT outperforming others on HUPD likely due to USPTO pretraining data).
